answer: Bind each seat to a named well in a real oasis. Each epoch the keeper lowers a whistle on a measured thread and records the echo: its ringing tail carries the shaft shape, its lining cracks, the water level, and a conductivity log. Seepage keeps the echo drifting, so no archive replays. Wells share an aquifer, so neighbours cross-sign; a false seat must forge a shaft that never existed. Cost per identity: a real well, a resident keeper, and hours of hauling thread and whistle, scaling linearly and not rentable. Two seats on one well return identical echoes; both bonds are slashed.
